title: Factors Associated With the Autonomy of Patients Treated by Haemodialysis in Community Centres. A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In France, haemodialysis is delivered in different settings depending on patients' health status and autonomy. Community centres include self-care and satellite units, which vary in organisation and patient involvement. OBJECTIVES: To describe the characteristics of patients treated in haemodialysis community centres and to identify factors associated with autonomy in self-care units. DESIGN: Cross-sectional study. PARTICIPANTS: All patients receiving haemodialysis in community centres in a French region on December 31, 2021. MEASUREMENTS: Patient characteristics and multiple dimensions of patient autonomy were recorded. Multivariate analyses assessed associations between patient factors and technical autonomy. RESULTS: Among 507 patients, 304 were treated in self-care units and 203 in satellite haemodialysis units. Patients in satellite haemodialysis units had a median age of 69 years (IQR 59-78; range 24-90), compared with 66 years (IQR 54-75; range 22-91) in self-care haemodialysis units. They also had more comorbidities. Younger age was associated with greater autonomy in arteriovenous fistula puncture-site dressing (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.96-0.98), setting the haemodialysis machine (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.96-0.98), and programming it (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.95-0.98). Autonomy differed significantly between centres, with centre affiliation significantly associated (p < .001) with autonomy for the arteriovenous fistula puncture-site dressing and machine-related tasks. CONCLUSIONS: Patient characteristics in self-care haemodialysis units did not fully explain autonomy for haemodialysis tasks. Considerable variability between centres was observed, suggesting that centre-related factors may contribute to differences in patient autonomy.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: In France, haemodialysis is delivered in different settings depending on patients' health status and autonomy. Community centres include self-care and satellite units, which vary in organisation and patient involvement. OBJECTIVES: To describe the characteristics of patients treated in haemodialysis community centres and to identify factors associated with autonomy in self-care units.

title: The complexity of provoked venous thromboembolism: one treatment plan does not fit all.
abstract: The decision of whether to continue patients diagnosed with venous thromboembolism (VTE) on anticoagulation after the initial treatment period is often nuanced. Many patients will have ≥1 transient risk factor associated with a time-limited increased risk of VTE. Transient risk factors are further divided into major factors, such as joint replacement, or minor factors, such as prolonged travel, which determine the magnitude of risk for an initial VTE. In addition, major transient risk factors generally carry a lower risk of recurrent VTE than minor transient risk factors. However, many patients will also have ≥1 persistent VTE risk factor, which further increase the risk for recurrence. Some persistent risk factors, such as inflammatory bowel disease, are associated with a sufficiently high risk of recurrent VTE, for which guidelines recommend indefinite anticoagulation. There are multiple other persistent risk factors that carry a lower risk of recurrent VTE, such as chronic renal insufficiency and obesity. The HI-PRO (High-Risk Patients with Provoked Venous Thromboembolism) trial sought to assess the efficacy and safety of extended thromboprophylaxis for the prevention of recurrent VTE in patients with an initial provoked VTE and at least 1 persistent risk factor. The study found a lower risk of recurrent VTE in the thromboprophylaxis cohort, challenging the traditional time-limited treatment for provoked VTE, but heterogeneity of the study population and small sample size preclude identification of which subsets of patients could safely discontinue anticoagulation. We consider the conundrum of provoked VTE in this review.

Many patients will have ≥1 transient risk factor associated with a time-limited increased risk of VTE. title: Changes in Long-Term Care Needs, Healthcare Costs, and Mortality Risk After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Japan: The Longevity Improvement & Fair Evidence Study.
abstract: AIM: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is increasingly performed in older adults with severe aortic stenosis, but there is limited evidence on their post-procedure changes in care needs, healthcare costs, and mortality risk. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used linked medical and long-term care (LTC) insurance claims data from 1361 patients aged ≥ 75 years who underwent TAVI in 13 Japanese municipalities. Patients were stratified into four groups by baseline certified care needs level: Independent (n = 725), Support Level 1-2 (n = 321), LTC Level 1-2 (n = 208), and LTC Level 3-5 (n = 107). RESULTS: Among 532 patients in the 36-month observation cohort, 53% were independent at baseline, and approximately half of those remained independent at 36 months. Monthly total medical and LTC costs at 36 months were approximately 5 times higher in the LTC Level 3-5 group than the Independent group. The LTC Level 3-5 group also showed significantly higher all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 3.19, 95% confidence interval 2.18-4.67). CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline care needs are associated with poorer outcomes and higher costs after TAVI. Incorporating care needs levels into clinical assessments may inform clinical decision-making and resource planning in older populations.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used linked medical and long-term care (LTC) insurance claims data from 1361 patients aged ≥ 75 years who underwent TAVI in 13 Japanese municipalities. Patients were stratified into four groups by baseline certified care needs level: Independent (n = 725), Support Level 1-2 (n = 321), LTC Level 1-2 (n = 208), and LTC Level 3-5 (n = 107).

title: A Versatile, Patient-Centred Approach to Surgical Wound Closure: A Single-Centre Case Series on the Use of a Synthetic Electrospun Fibre Matrix in Vasculopathic Patients.
abstract: Patients with vascular disease often suffer from lower extremity ulcerations that may require surgical intervention to remove non-viable or infected tissues. Post-operatively, these patients still present with a high risk of non-healing due to poor blood flow and chronic inflammation. Advanced wound healing matrices may be considered to support tissue regenerative and reduce the risk of further wound complications. A synthetic electrospun fibre matrix (SEFM) (Restrata, Acera Surgical Inc.) is a fully synthetic, extracellular matrix that encourages cellular infiltration and neovascularization with minimal inflammatory response. In the present study, a single vascular surgeon retrospectively reviewed data of vasculopathic patients treated with SEFM during surgical management of various wound aetiologies. Ten patients were identified and data on time to closure, closure approach and post-operative complications were collected and analysed. SEFM was utilized to either support neo-vascularization for subsequent autografting or re-epithelialization through secondary intention healing. All patients in this series achieved either definitive closure or complete re-epithelialization in an average of 6.8 weeks. One instance of superficial infection was successfully managed with antibiotics. No instances of unplanned re-operation or other wound complications were observed. Early experience suggests practical application of SEFM for surgical wound management in vasculopathic patients.

Post-operatively, these patients still present with a high risk of non-healing due to poor blood flow and chronic inflammation. Advanced wound healing matrices may be considered to support tissue regenerative and reduce the risk of further wound complications.

title: Effectiveness of Tomazoni Measurement Method for Central Catheter Tip Positioning in Neonates: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) tip positioning in neonates remains challenging, with high rates of malposition reported using traditional measurement methods. AIM: To evaluate the effectiveness of the Tomazoni method for PICC positioning in neonates compared with the traditional method. STUDY DESIGN: Pragmatic, parallel-group randomised clinical trial with stratified block randomisation, conducted in a neonatal intensive care unit in Brazil between June 2024 and April 2025. RESULTS: Of 62 randomised procedures, 55 were evaluable (27 in the experimental group, 28 in the control group). Central positioning was achieved in 21 of 27 procedures (77.8%) in the experimental group versus 5 of 28 (17.9%) in the control group (p < 0.001). PICC insertion procedures assessed using the Tomazoni method were 4.36 times more likely to achieve central tip placement (RR = 4.36; 95% CI: 1.91-9.88). Catheter withdrawal was required in 3 of 27 procedures (11.1%) in the experimental group versus 16 of 28 (57.1%) in the control group (p = 0.001; RR = 0.19; 95% CI: 0.06-0.59). CONCLUSIONS: The Tomazoni measurement method was associated with substantially higher rates of central PICC tip positioning and reduced need for catheter withdrawal compared with the traditional method. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: The Tomazoni method offers a reproducible, low-cost measurement strategy that can be implemented in neonatal intensive care units to improve catheter positioning accuracy and reduce procedure-related manipulations, with potential implications for patient safety. The trial, titled 'Comparison between measurements of peripherally inserted central catheters in children and newborns', was registered in the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry under the identifier RBR-55zwb45. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial is registered in the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry (ReBEC) under the identifier RBR-55zwb45.

AIM: To evaluate the effectiveness of the Tomazoni method for PICC positioning in neonates compared with the traditional method. STUDY DESIGN: Pragmatic, parallel-group randomised clinical trial with stratified block randomisation, conducted in a neonatal intensive care unit in Brazil between June 2024 and April 2025.

title: Reducing Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections in ICUs: A Systematic Review of Barriers and Facilitators and Intervention Measures.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite established guidelines, central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) remains a severe ICU complication due to cognitive and resource barriers hindering healthcare worker compliance. A systematic evaluation of these barriers and facilitators is currently lacking but is important for informing targeted implementation strategies for CLABSI prevention. AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators to implementing CLABSI prevention in ICUs using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to provide evidence-based strategies for improvement. STUDY DESIGN: A PRISMA-guided systematic review was performed using PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, Wan fang, and CBM databases, up to August 2026. Eligible studies included qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-methods research on the barriers and facilitators to CLABSI prevention implementation among ICU healthcare workers. Two researchers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Data synthesis and intervention development were guided by the CFIR, with targeted strategies mapped using the CFIR-ERIC (Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change) matching tool. RESULTS: The literature search identified 1,780 records, of which 28 studies were ultimately included. The review identified 28 barriers and facilitators, which were synthesized into four major themes and mapped to 16 CFIR constructs across the catheter-care continuum. The most prominent barriers involved staff knowledge gaps, inconsistent adherence to recommended practices, limited resources, and insufficient leadership support. CFIR-ERIC mapping identified 11 Level 1 expert-endorsed implementation strategies, of which four were represented in the included literature and seven were identified as potential implementation gaps. CONCLUSIONS: CLABSI prevention in ICUs is influenced by multilevel implementation determinants spanning individual, organizational, and practice-related factors. A structured implementation-science approach may help healthcare organizations identify context-specific barriers and prioritize targeted strategies to support more consistent implementation of evidence-based CLABSI prevention practices. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Improving CLABSI prevention may require multilevel strategies that combine targeted education and training, adequate resource allocation, leadership engagement, standardized clinical procedures, and ongoing audit and feedback. These strategies may help strengthen adherence to evidence-based practices, improve quality of care, and enhance patient safety in ICUs.

A systematic evaluation of these barriers and facilitators is currently lacking but is important for informing targeted implementation strategies for CLABSI prevention. AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators to implementing CLABSI prevention in ICUs using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to provide evidence-based strategies for improvement.

title: [The Heart Team as a multidisciplinary approach to the management of patients eligible for surgical and transcatheter treatment of aortic valve disease - Consensus document].
abstract: Aortic valve disease, particularly severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, represents a growing public health problem due to the aging population. The increasing complexity of managing this condition - driven by the evolution of surgical and transcatheter techniques and the expansion of treatment indications - requires a multidisciplinary organizational model capable of ensuring quality and safety of care. This consensus document, jointly developed by AGENAS and the leading Italian scientific societies involved in the management of valvular heart disease, defines the principles for the implementation and functioning of the Heart Team as a central element of the decision-making process for patients undergoing evaluation for surgical aortic valve replacement or transcatheter aortic valve implantation. The document describes the composition, responsibilities, and operational procedures of the Heart Team, highlighting the importance of multidisciplinary assessment, patient-tailored treatment, shared decision-making with the patient, and outcome monitoring. The aim is to promote a standardized organizational model across the country, aligned with the scientific evidence and the most recent international guidelines, thereby contributing to improved clinical outcomes and greater efficiency of the Italian National Health Service.

title: [Abdominal aortic aneurysms: diagnosis, risk stratification and treatment strategies].
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm is defined as a focal aortic dilation ≥3.0 cm in maximum diameter, with rupture-associated mortality approaching 80%. Anatomical classification identifies infrarenal (80%), juxtarenal, pararenal and suprarenal aneurysms. Operative thresholds are 5.5 cm in men and 5.0 cm in women. Endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) provides an early survival benefit, with 30-day mortality of 1.8% vs 4.3% for open repair in the EVAR-1 trial, and substantially comparable long-term outcomes up to 15 years of follow-up, at the cost of a 15-20% reintervention burden and the need for lifelong imaging surveillance. Accordingly, the 2024 European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines consider EVAR as the preferred treatment in most patients with favorable anatomy, reserving open repair for young patients with long life expectancy, unfavorable anatomy and specific conditions such as connective tissue disease, inflammatory aneurysms, graft infection and failed previous endovascular repair. Treatment selection should be based on the integrated assessment of individual operative risk, aortic anatomy and life expectancy.

Anatomical classification identifies infrarenal (80%), juxtarenal, pararenal and suprarenal aneurysms. Operative thresholds are 5.5 cm in men and 5.0 cm in women.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Apixaban Thromboprophylaxis According to Baseline Chemotherapy Class in High-Risk Ambulatory Cancer Patients: A Post Hoc Analysis of the AVERT Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in cancer patients. The AVERT trial showed apixaban thromboprophylaxis reduced VTE in intermediate-to-high-risk patients initiating chemotherapy. However, the efficacy and safety of apixaban according to baseline chemotherapy class remain incompletely characterized. METHODS: We conducted a post hoc analysis stratified by chemotherapy class of the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled AVERT trial comparing apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) with placebo in ambulatory cancer patients initiating chemotherapy. The primary efficacy outcome was VTE, and the primary safety outcome was clinically relevant bleeding (major or clinically relevant non major bleeding (CRNMB)) per ISTH criteria. A subgroup analysis compared platinum-based with non-platinum chemotherapy. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI), adjusted for age, sex, and study site. Treatment-by-platinum interaction terms were used to assess effect modification by platinum exposure. RESULTS: A total of 563 patients were included and categorized by one or more chemotherapy classes at randomization. Compared with placebo, apixaban appeared to reduce VTE in patients on platinum (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.16-0.57), taxane (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.23-0.75), taxane-platinum (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.12-0.68), topoisomerase inhibitor (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.19-0.53), and antimetabolite regimens (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.12-0.54), without increased bleeding. Among placebo-treated patients, platinum-based chemotherapy was associated with a higher risk of VTE compared with non-platinum regimens (HR 2.25, 95% CI 1.48-3.42), whereas no statistically significant difference was observed among apixaban-treated patients. Treatment-by-platinum interaction testing did not demonstrate significant effect modification by platinum exposure. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis, apixaban thromboprophylaxis was associated with reduced VTE across several chemotherapy regimens with generally acceptable safety outcomes. Patients receiving platinum-based chemotherapy may derive greater absolute benefit from thromboprophylaxis in the setting of higher underlying thrombotic risk.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in cancer patients. The AVERT trial showed apixaban thromboprophylaxis reduced VTE in intermediate-to-high-risk patients initiating chemotherapy. However, the efficacy and safety of apixaban according to baseline chemotherapy class remain incompletely characterized.

title: Underdetected peripheral artery disease in people with hypertension: A narrative review of risk-stratified case-finding, diagnostic pathways, and equity in care.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is common but often underrecognized in people with hypertension because symptoms are frequently absent or atypical and access to physiologic testing is uneven. This narrative review examines how hypertension care can support risk-stratified PAD recognition while keeping targeted case-finding distinct from universal screening. METHODS: We conducted a structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE from inception through 31 July 2026, supplemented by citation searching and review of major US and European guidelines and relevant US policy and coverage sources. Evidence was interpreted according to the question it could answer: association/prognosis, diagnostic accuracy, treatment effect, implementation, or policy status. RESULTS: Hypertension and PAD share age-related, metabolic, renal, and tobacco-related determinants, while pressure-related vascular injury provides biological plausibility for their association. Resting ankle-brachial index (ABI) is the initial physiologic test for appropriately selected people; toe-brachial index with waveforms is preferred for noncompressible ankle arteries, exercise ABI for persistent exertional symptoms despite normal or borderline resting values, and duplex ultrasound when anatomic definition will change management. Guideline-supported risk-based testing differs from universal screening of unselected asymptomatic adults, for which outcome benefit remains unproven. Detection is clinically meaningful only when linked to appropriate prevention, symptom management, foot protection, and referral. CONCLUSION: This narrative review supports a risk-stratified, treatment-linked approach to PAD recognition in hypertension care, but the proposed case-finding pathway itself has not been proven to improve clinical outcomes. Pragmatic trials of the complete care pathway are needed.

METHODS: We conducted a structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE from inception through 31 July 2026, supplemented by citation searching and review of major US and European guidelines and relevant US policy and coverage sources.

title: Comparison of 1-year costs of commercially insured patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing surgical vs. transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with aortic stenosis (AS) have been shown to have lower costs at 1 year with transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) compared with surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in a Medicare population. The difference in costs between TAVR and SAVR in commercially insured patients with AS in the United States is unknown. METHODS: Using the Optum claims database, AS patients receiving either TAVR or SAVR between 3/2019 and 9/2022 were identified. Patients were categorized into low, intermediate or high strata using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS). The primary outcome was total 1-year cost, defined as the sum of index AVR hospitalization and 1-year follow-up costs. Risk-adjusted generalized linear models were used to assess the difference in the costs between TAVR and SAVR. RESULTS: p p p p p p 3,623 patients (952 TAVR; 2,671 SAVR) were identified. TAVR patients had lower index hospitalization costs compared with SAVR patients across all HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $39,312, < 0.01; intermediate: $42,006, < 0.01; high: $39,431, = 0.03). Cumulative costs through one year were significantly lower with TAVR in the low and intermediate HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $32,116, < 0.01; intermediate $40,905, < 0.01) and numerically lower in the high HFRS stratum (cost difference: $35,881, = 0.15). When the analysis was restricted to isolated AVR, the 1-year difference was no longer significant in the low and intermediate HFRS strata ($8,064 and $11,314, respectively) and was numerically reversed in the high HFRS stratum (-$28,804). CONCLUSIONS: In a commercial payor population of real-world patients with AS, TAVR was associated with lower standardized index hospitalization costs across all HFRS strata and lower standardized 1-year costs in the low and intermediate HFRS strata. These findings demonstrate that baseline frailty and procedural scope are critical determinants of short and intermediate-term cost differences between TAVR and SAVR for the treatment of AS in commercial populations.

The difference in costs between TAVR and SAVR in commercially insured patients with AS in the United States is unknown. METHODS: Using the Optum claims database, AS patients receiving either TAVR or SAVR between 3/2019 and 9/2022 were identified.

title: In-Hospital Outcomes and Mortality After Revascularization for Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia by Maintenance Dialysis Status: A National Inpatient Sample Analysis, 2006-2020.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Evidence on in-hospital outcomes after chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) revascularization in patients receiving maintenance dialysis is limited. METHODS: We analyzed adult CMI-coded hospitalizations undergoing endovascular or open revascularization in the 2006-2020 National Inpatient Sample. Hospitalizations with and without maintenance dialysis were compared using 1:2 propensity score matching and survey-weighted multivariable regression. RESULTS: Of 7,962 eligible hospitalizations, 411 (5.2% of the unweighted sample) involved maintenance dialysis. Maintenance dialysis was associated with higher adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.96), non-routine discharge (aOR 1.46), prolonged hospitalization (aOR 1.41), transfusion (aOR 1.43), sepsis (aOR 1.88), pneumonia (aOR 1.69), multiorgan failure or shock (aOR 1.80), and venous thromboembolism (aOR 2.06). Hospital charges were also higher (adjusted beta USD 17,497), whereas urinary tract infection odds were lower (aOR 0.68). DISCUSSION: Maintenance dialysis was associated with greater in-hospital morbidity and mortality among CMI-coded revascularization hospitalizations. The inability to distinguish stable from acute-on-chronic CMI limits interpretation as an elective cohort. Findings support individualized perioperative assessment without establishing causation or optimal treatment timing.

METHODS: We analyzed adult CMI-coded hospitalizations undergoing endovascular or open revascularization in the 2006-2020 National Inpatient Sample. Hospitalizations with and without maintenance dialysis were compared using 1:2 propensity score matching and survey-weighted multivariable regression.

title: Maternal and Fetal Safety Outcomes of Thrombolytics for Ischemic Stroke in Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Aggregated Case Series.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The safety of intravenous thrombolytics for ischemic stroke in pregnancy is largely unknown. We performed a systematic review to identify published use of thrombolytics for stroke during pregnancy, with the aim of assessing maternal and fetal safety outcomes. To provide additional safety data, we included cases of thrombolysis for deep vein thrombosis, mechanical valve thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism in pregnancy. METHODS: We used the PRISMA and MOOSE guidelines to conduct the review. We searched 3 databases (OVID Medline, EMBASE, Scopus) for studies published up to October 2025. We analyzed outcomes in a Bayesian aggregated case series to compare rates of adverse outcomes in our cohort with those in the general population. Elective termination and spontaneous abortion were grouped together, given that it was often difficult to determine whether complications of thrombolysis may have played a role in the decision for termination. RESULTS: We included 123 studies of 216 patients (median age 31 years) treated with thrombolytics during pregnancy, of whom 85 had ischemic stroke. Six of the 32 total fetal deaths were deemed likely to be causally related to thrombolytics (3 in stroke). The risk of miscarriage in our thrombolysis population was 12.4% higher (95% credible interval [CrI]: 2.6%, 23.2%) than published general pregnant population rates, and the risk of stillbirth was 5.9% higher (95% CrI: 1.6%, 12.7%). The proportion of pregnant patients with symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage was similar between our pregnant cohort and young, nonpregnant patients receiving thrombolytics (risk difference -0.4%; 95% CrI: -0.8%, 2.7%). DISCUSSION: Thrombolytics were likely causally associated with a small minority of published cases of fetal death after thrombolysis in pregnancy. There was no signal of increased harm from thrombolysis to the mother, including similar rates of symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage. In many cases, it was difficult to discern effects of thrombolytics on fetal outcomes from the effects of the disease itself; hence, our results should be interpreted with caution. Nonetheless, our findings broadly support the use of thrombolytics in otherwise-eligible pregnant patients but underscore the importance of the risk-benefit assessment in such patients. TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: The study protocol was pre-registered on PROSPERO (registration number: CRD42024605043).

To provide additional safety data, we included cases of thrombolysis for deep vein thrombosis, mechanical valve thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism in pregnancy.

title: T-cell states in aortic dissection: from molecular immune profiling toward causal and translational validation.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Single-cell RNA sequencing and T-cell receptor profiling reveal substantial T-cell heterogeneity in aortic dissection (AD), but whether these responses contribute to vascular injury or reflect post-onset immune activation remains uncertain. This review evaluates human and experimental evidence by disease stage, tissue compartment, functional validation, T-cell specificity, and intervention timing, distinguishing descriptive profiling from evidence supporting causal and translational inference. DISCUSSION: + Human studies identify Th1/Th17-associated, CD8cytotoxicity-associated, and regulatory T-cell alterations, with stage-related differences in T-cell composition and clonality. Most evidence is cross-sectional and obtained after clinical onset. Antigen specificity, direct aortic-wall cytotoxicity, impaired Treg suppression, and T-cell-mediated aortic-wall injury remain unproven. Single-cell and TCR profiling identify candidate T-cell states and clonotypes for spatial and functional validation, not causal proof. Among candidate pathways, the IL-6-STAT3-IL-17 axis currently has the strongest AD-specific preclinical rationale, but existing interventions are largely non-T-cell-restricted and initiated before or during disease induction. Stronger causal attribution requires convergent human evidence, post-lesion T-cell-restricted perturbation, disease-progression endpoints, and rescue or target-engagement studies. The subacute phase after anatomical and haemodynamic stabilisation may offer a window to study persistent injury-amplifying T-cell responses, whereas early acute and perioperative immunomodulation remains unsupported. CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports altered T-cell states after AD onset but does not establish an initiating role. Near-term priorities should be prospective biomarker validation and post-lesion mechanistic studies rather than T-cell-directed immuno-modulation during the early acute and perioperative phases. Clinical translation should await reproducible associations linked to stage-specific causal mechanisms and acceptable safety.

title: High-intensity focused ultrasound as a bridging vascular-modulating therapy for fertility-sparing management of placental site trophoblastic tumor complicated by uterine arteriovenous fistula: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Placental site trophoblastic tumor (PSTT) is a rare gestational trophoblastic neoplasm characterized by local invasiveness and marked vascularity. Surgical management may be associated with substantial bleeding risk and loss of fertility, particularly when complicated by uterine arteriovenous fistula (UAVF). High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) may provide a fertility-preserving adjunctive approach in selected cases. CASE PRESENTATION: A 23-year-old woman presented with persistently plateaued serum human chorionic gonadotropin levels following hysteroscopic management for suspected incomplete abortion. Imaging revealed a deeply invasive hypervascular uterine lesion with UAVF, raising strong suspicion of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. Given her strong desire for fertility preservation and high surgical risk, ultrasound-guided HIFU was performed as an initial vascular-modulating intervention. Subsequent expert pathological review confirmed PSTT. RESULTS: HIFU achieved significant reduction in lesion perfusion and vascular flow, as confirmed by Doppler ultrasound and contrast-enhanced MRI. Although complete tumor ablation was not achieved due to lesion size and deep invasion, subsequent low-dose chemotherapy resulted in complete biochemical remission accompanied by radiologic regression of residual lesions. No major HIFU-related complications were observed, and normal menstrual function resumed during follow-up. CONCLUSION: HIFU is a technically feasible and safe fertility-preserving adjunct for vascular modulation in hypervascular PSTT complicated by UAVF. While HIFU alone may not achieve definitive oncologic control in large or deeply invasive lesions, it can serve as a bridging strategy to reduce tumor perfusion and vascularity, facilitating subsequent systemic therapy in carefully selected patients. This approach demonstrates the potential role of HIFU as a bridging vascular-modulating strategy within multimodal fertility-preserving management.

Surgical management may be associated with substantial bleeding risk and loss of fertility, particularly when complicated by uterine arteriovenous fistula (UAVF). High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) may provide a fertility-preserving adjunctive approach in selected cases.

title: Pregnancy and iron deficiency anemia are associated with COVID-19 severity: a retrospective cohort study from Gaza.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: COVID-19 poses significant risks to pregnant women, with pregnancy recognized as a risk factor for severe disease. This vulnerability may be exacerbated by iron deficiency anemia (IDA) due to impaired immune function, reduced oxygen transport, and altered coagulation and endothelial function. METHODS: n n A retrospective cohort study of 271 unvaccinated, otherwise healthy women aged 18-38 with COVID-19 was conducted at Al-Shifa Hospital, Gaza (2021). Pregnant ( = 97) and nonpregnant ( = 174) groups were stratified by IDA, investigating the impact of pregnancy and IDA on the severity of COVID-19. Iron deficiency was determined by transferrin saturation levels <20% measured during acute infection, whereas ferritin levels were not available. RESULTS: p p p p p p p p Overall pregnancy was significantly associated with COVID-19 severity ( < 0.001), with pregnant women having higher odds of critical illness (OR = 4.61, 95% CI 2.27-9.39, < 0.001) and death (OR = 5.25, 95% CI 1.91-14.44, = 0.001) compared with moderate illness. All deaths were due to acute respiratory distress syndrome; no venous thromboembolism cases occurred. IDA was associated with COVID-19 severity in both pregnant ( = 0.015) and non-pregnant ( = 0.002) women. In a multivariable model including pregnancy, IDA was associated with higher odds of severe (OR = 3.57, 95% CI 1.97-6.48, < 0.001), critical (OR = 2.25, 95% CI 1.09-4.64, = 0.029), and fatal illness (OR = 7.23, 95% CI 1.96-26.74, = 0.003) compared with moderate illness. CONCLUSION: This study suggests that among young, otherwise healthy, unvaccinated women with COVID-19, pregnancy and IDA are associated with increased COVID-19 severity. However, interpretation requires caution considering the small number of events, particularly deaths, and the assessment of iron status during acute infection using transferrin saturation alone without ferritin measurements, which limits the ability to distinguish preexisting iron deficiency from inflammation-related changes in iron metabolism.

title: Association between neuromuscular electrical stimulation and intermittent pneumatic compression for the prevention of deep venous thrombosis among neurosurgery patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) considerably affects the incidence and mortality rates in patients undergoing neurosurgery. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) and intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) are frequently used as adjunct treatments to prevent DVT; however, their effects remain unclear. This study was conducted to compare the association of NMES and IPC as two mechanical prophylaxis strategies in neurosurgical patients who were ineligible for pharmacological prophylaxis. METHODS: Postoperative neurosurgical patients were retrospectively enrolled from a single centre between January 2020 and December 2021. These patients were assessed to have a high bleeding risk and received either NMES or IPC as mechanical prophylaxis. Univariable analysis was used to explore the risk factors for DVT, and multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to determine the independent associations between DVT and potential variables after adjusting for confounding factors. RESULTS: p p p p Among 232 patients who underwent neurosurgery, 131 received IPC and 101 received NMES, with no overlap between the two groups. DVT was diagnosed in 62 patients (11 received NMES and 51 received IPC). After controlling for sex, age, operation duration and length of hospital stay, NMES use was associated with a lower incidence of DVT (OR = 0.268, 95% CI = 0.125-0.576, = .001). Moreover, men were less likely to have DVT than women (OR = 0.469, 95% CI = 0.242-0.910, = .025), older age was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 3.419, 95% CI = 1.594-7.334, = .002), and a longer operation duration was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 2.180, 95% CI = 1.042-4.560, = .039). CONCLUSION: This study found an association between NMES and reduced odds of DVT compared with IPC in neurosurgery patients. Although NMES may be more widely adopted in neurosurgery to decrease the incidence of DVT, further evidence is required to determine its effectiveness in clinical practice.

title: Adipsic Hypernatremia Complicated by Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State and Extensive Venous Thromboembolism After Traumatic Brain Injury: A Case Report.
abstract: Adipsic hypernatremia is a rare disorder characterized by impaired thirst perception despite severe hyperosmolality, most commonly resulting from hypothalamic dysfunction. Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state (HHS) may further aggravate dehydration and electrolyte imbalance, increasing the risk of neurologic injury, acute kidney injury (AKI), and thromboembolic complications. Reports describing the coexistence of adipsic hypernatremia, HHS, and extensive venous thromboembolism are limited. A 42-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes and recent traumatic brain injury presented with neurologic decline, severe dehydration without thirst, severe hypernatremia, HHS, and transient renal dysfunction consistent with prerenal injury. Persistent severe hypernatremia despite improvement in hyperglycemia, together with preserved urinary concentrating ability, supported adipsic hypernatremia. Further evaluation revealed extensive deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and bilateral pulmonary embolism (PE), while brain imaging showed only mild diffuse cerebral atrophy. The patient was treated with controlled volume and free-water replacement, intravenous insulin therapy, anticoagulation, and close monitoring of serum sodium, glucose, renal function, and urine output. Gradual correction of hypernatremia resulted in significant improvement in neurologic manifestations, renal function, and metabolic abnormalities. Following stabilization, he was discharged on apixaban therapy with scheduled oral hydration instructions and outpatient follow-up. This case highlights a possible synergistic interaction between adipsic hypernatremia and HHS, which may have contributed to severe hyperosmolar stress and extensive thromboembolic complications. Adipsic hypernatremia should be considered in patients with severe hypernatremia and absent thirst sensation, particularly after traumatic brain injury, even when neuroimaging findings are unremarkable.

Reports describing the coexistence of adipsic hypernatremia, HHS, and extensive venous thromboembolism are limited.

title: Nurse-led, multidisciplinary strategies to reduce central line-associated bloodstream infections: Parenteral nutrition stewardship and central venous access device maintenance.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSIs) remain a major source of preventable patient harm and are associated with increased mortality, longer hospital stays, and higher health care costs. Reducing central venous access device (CVAD) utilization and improving line maintenance practices are key strategies for prevention. PURPOSE: To reduce CLABSIs through a nurse-led, multidisciplinary initiative focused on parenteral nutrition (PN) stewardship, CVAD maintenance, and shared accountability for line necessity and care. METHODS: Using Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles, an interprofessional team implemented a PN clinical decision tree, standardized PN administration kit, targeted nursing education, daily multidisciplinary line rounds, and real-time escalation processes. Outcomes included CLABSI Standardized Infection Ratio (SIR), Standardized Utilization Ratio (SUR), PN-related CLABSIs, and adherence to line care practices. RESULTS: The initiative was associated with a 46% reduction in CLABSI SIR (1.165-0.632), an 11.7% reduction in CVAD utilization (SUR 0.479-0.423; P < .001), and a decrease in PN-related CLABSIs from 45% to 12.5% of all CLABSI cases. Process-related issues identified during rounds decreased from 32.73% to 26.11%. CONCLUSIONS: A nurse-led, multidisciplinary approach combining PN stewardship, standardized CVAD care, and real-time feedback improved patient safety and reduced CLABSI risk. The model offers a sustainable, replicable strategy for infection prevention.

PURPOSE: To reduce CLABSIs through a nurse-led, multidisciplinary initiative focused on parenteral nutrition (PN) stewardship, CVAD maintenance, and shared accountability for line necessity and care.

title: Cross-elbow stent placement for refractory arteriovenous fistula stenosis and chronic total occlusion in hemodialysis patients: a single-center retrospective cohort of 42 cases.
abstract: Cross-elbow stent placement in hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) has been avoided due to risks of fracture, kinking, deformation, migration, and infection. However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage. Consecutive adult hemodialysis patients who received cross-elbow stents for clinically significant AVF stenosis or CTO (September 2021 - March 2026) at a single center were retrospectively analyzed. Primary outcomes were target lesion primary patency (TLPP), access circuit primary patency (ACPP), access circuit secondary patency, and access circuit assisted primary patency, estimated by Kaplan-Meier. Technical and clinical success and complications were recorded. Forty-two patients were included; 45.2% had CTO and 57.1% had prior PTA. Eluvia-based stents were used in 83.3%. Technical and clinical success were both 100%. Mean access flow increased from 407 ± 267 to 839 ± 188 mL/min. TLPP at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months was 90.1%, 84.4%, 76.9%, and 76.9%, respectively. No stent fracture, migration, kinking, or infection occurred. Cross-elbow stenting was technically feasible and provided favorable short- to mid-term patency without device-related complications, supporting its use as a salvage option for selected refractory AVF lesions and CTOs.

However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage.

title: Use of vaginal estrogens in urogynecology: current evidence, controversies and clinical applications.
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) is a prevalent yet underrecognized condition in postmenopausal women, characterized by progressive vulvovaginal and lower urinary tract symptoms from estrogen deficiency. Vaginal estrogen therapy is the first-line pharmacologic treatment for GSM. However, as new evidence emerges, understanding of its efficacy, safety, and use in special populations continues to evolve. This review summarizes current evidence on vaginal estrogen formulations, clinical effectiveness, safety, and therapeutic applications. RECENT FINDINGS: Recent randomized controlled trials confirm that low-dose vaginal estrogen significantly improves GSM symptoms - including vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, and irritation - while restoring epithelial integrity and normalizing pH. Evidence also supports its role in reducing recurrent urinary tract infections by restoring lactobacilli-dominant flora, reinforced by a 2025 multisociety clinical guideline recommending topical, but not systemic, estrogen for this indication. Comparative studies show similar efficacy across creams, tablets, inserts, and rings, differing primarily in convenience and absorption rather than effectiveness. Large cohort studies indicate no increased risk of cardiovascular disease, venous thromboembolism, or malignancy. Use in breast cancer survivors remains controversial, but emerging data suggest minimal systemic absorption and no clear increase in recurrence risk, supporting shared decision-making. In addition, long-term outcomes show that adjunctive vaginal estrogen does not improve anatomic surgical success after native tissue apical prolapse repair. Nonhormonal therapies and agents like ospemifene or prasterone offer alternative options, though they demonstrate lower or more variable efficacy than vaginal estrogen. SUMMARY: Vaginal estrogen therapy is the most effective, evidence-based treatment for GSM and helps prevent recurrent urinary tract infections in postmenopausal women. Its favorable safety profile and multiple formulations enable individualized care. Recent evidence clarifies that while overall safety is reassuring, caution is necessary for breast cancer survivors using aromatase inhibitors. Additionally, longer-term perioperative trial data temper expectations regarding surgical-recurrence benefits, while confirming its value for local tissue optimization. Ongoing research should focus on long-term safety in high-risk groups and the effectiveness of emerging non-estrogen alternatives.

However, as new evidence emerges, understanding of its efficacy, safety, and use in special populations continues to evolve.

title: Trends in incident hemodialysis access and mortality in China: results from China Renal Data System 2000-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUNDS: Large‑scale multicenter data on vascular access among Chinese incident hemodialysis (HD) patients are limited. We explored temporal trends of initial vascular access and its relationship with all‑cause mortality. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted using the China Renal Data System, enrolling incident HD patients from January 2000 to April 2024. Vascular access trends and distribution at HD initiation were analyzed. RESULTS: 16,717 patients were enrolled (mean age 55.62 ± 10.93 years; 61.54% male; mean follow‑up 64.41 months). At HD initiation, 29.17% of patients used arteriovenous fistula/graft (AVF/AVG), while 70.83% used central venous catheter (CVC), comprising 60.78% with a maturing AVF/AVG and 10.06% with CVC alone. AVF/AVG use increased from 26.24% in 2015 to 35.77% in 2024, while CVC-only use decreased from 16.16% to 8.27%. Mortality rates per 100 person-years were 4.15 (95% confidence interval [CI] 3.93 - 4.38), 7.24 (95% CI 7.00 - 7.49), and 15.08 (95% CI 14.07 - 16.15) in the AVF/AVG, CVC with maturing AVF/AVG, and CVC-only groups, respectively. In the adjusted Cox model, patients using CVC with a maturing AVF/AVG or CVC alone exhibited 36% and 91% higher all-cause mortality risks, respectively, compared with those using AVF/AVG. CONCLUSIONS: Over the 25-year period, initial vascular access among Chinese incident HD patients gradually shifted from CVC to AVF/AVG, reflecting ongoing and considerable improvements in vascular access practice in China. CVC use at HD initiation was associated with higher all-cause mortality compared with AVF/AVG. These findings support early AVF/AVG creation in end-stage kidney disease patients to avoid CVC use at HD initiation.

We explored temporal trends of initial vascular access and its relationship with all‑cause mortality. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted using the China Renal Data System, enrolling incident HD patients from January 2000 to April 2024.

title: Silymarin attenuates neuroinflammation after subarachnoid hemorrhage by inducing M2 microglial polarization via activation of the JAK1/STAT6 signaling pathway.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Neuroinflammation represents a key pathological process in early brain injury (EBI) following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and contributes significantly to poor outcomes. Silymarin, known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has been shown to exert neuroprotective effects. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain to be clarified. An in vivo endovascular perforation model and an in vitro hemoglobin-stimulated model were used to investigate the pharmacological effects of silymarin in SAH. Neurological function was assessed using SAH scores and neurobehavioral scores. Neuronal apoptosis was evaluated by TUNEL staining. Neuroinflammation was measured by ELISA or qPCR, and microglial polarization status was determined by assessing CD86 and CD206 expression via Western blotting (WB) or immunofluorescence (IF) staining. Ruxolitinib and AS1517499 were applied to block the JAK1/STAT6 pathway. Silymarin attenuated early brain injury (EBI) after SAH, as indicated by improved neurological scores, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and lower brain water content. In vivo, silymarin treatment was associated with JAK1/STAT6 activation, elevated M2 markers, and decreased pro‑inflammatory cytokines. In vitro, silymarin activated the JAK1/STAT6 pathway, promoted M2 microglial polarization, and suppressed inflammatory cytokine production. In addition, pharmacological blockade of JAK1/STAT6 reversed silymarin's protective effects, confirming a causal role of this pathway in the cellular context. Our in vitro data demonstrate that silymarin directly stimulates JAK1/STAT6 to drive M2 polarization and anti‑inflammatory responses. In vivo, we observed a correlation between pathway activation and neuroprotective benefits. Together, these findings provide a rationale for further exploring silymarin‑based therapies in SAH. title: Long-term outcome of stenting for the iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral arterio-venous graft; a case series.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the possible etiology and evaluate the technical and clinical outcomes of using bare metal stents for the treatment of central venous stenosis (CVS) in the lower extremity with ipsilateral hemodialysis access. METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis of a small case series was conducted in hemodialysis patients with lower extremity arteriovenous grafts (AVG) who were treated with bare metal stents (BMS) for symptomatic iliac vein stenosis between April 2016 and June 2021. Patients' demographic data, technical details, adverse events, clinical outcomes, and imaging data were recorded. RESULTS: The study cohort comprised seven females and four males, with a mean age of 58.8 ± 13.4 years. Preoperative lower limb venography was performed in nine patients scheduled for AVG creation. With the exception of one case demonstrating left iliac vein compression, the iliac veins were patent in all other patients. Symptoms of lower limb swelling developed at a mean interval of 9.40 ± 5.83 months (range: 3-20 months) following AVG placement. Eight cases had a concomitant history of temporary ipsilateral femoral vein catheterization. Lesion characteristics included nine stenotic lesions and two occlusive lesions. All patients were treated with SMART Control stents (Cordis Corp, USA). The technical success rate was 100%, and symptomatic relief was achieved in all cases. Over a mean follow-up period of 47.8 ± 31.7 months (range: 10-123 months), the target lesion primary patency was 100% (one-side confidence interval [CI] = 0.74,1). CONCLUSIONS: Using BMS is a safe and effective method to treat iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral AVG.

METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis of a small case series was conducted in hemodialysis patients with lower extremity arteriovenous grafts (AVG) who were treated with bare metal stents (BMS) for symptomatic iliac vein stenosis between April 2016 and June 2021. Patients' demographic data, technical details, adverse events, clinical outcomes, and imaging data were recorded.

title: Bilateral peripheral CT venography for evaluating central venous lesions in dysfunctional arteriovenous fistulas: feasibility, safety, and radiation dose in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Central venous stenosis and occlusion are major causes of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) dysfunction in hemodialysis patients. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, radiation exposure, and anatomical findings of bilateral peripheral CT venography for central venous assessment in patients with dysfunctional AVFs. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 46 consecutive hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs who underwent bilateral peripheral CT venography between August 2023 and June 2025. Technical success, procedure-related adverse events, radiation dose parameters, central venous lesion characteristics, and agreement with available comparative imaging modalities were analyzed. Comparative imaging findings from puncture-based angiography and/or duplex ultrasonography were assessed descriptively. RESULTS: All 46 examinations were technically successful (100%), with a mean procedure duration of 4 minutes (range, 3-5 minutes). Minor adverse events included one patient of contrast extravasation (2.2%) and 3 of mild allergic reactions (6.5%); no severe procedure-related complications were documented. The mean CTDIvol and DLP were 11.87 mGy and 784.15 mGy·cm, respectively. Central venous abnormalities were identified in 44 patients (95.7%), including stenosis in 31 (67.4%), occlusion in 11 (23.9%), and aneurysmal changes in 2 (4.3%). Comparative imaging was available in 38 patients, and CT venography showed agreement with available findings in 37 cases (97.4%). This agreement was interpreted as descriptive concordance rather than formal diagnostic accuracy. CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral peripheral CT venography demonstrated high technical feasibility, acceptable safety, and effective visualization of central venous abnormalities in hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs. Further prospective studies are needed to validate its diagnostic performance and clinical impact. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This technique enables efficient, noninvasive assessment of central venous pathology with minimal risk, supporting its potential as a practical alternative to conventional imaging in hemodialysis patients.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 46 consecutive hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs who underwent bilateral peripheral CT venography between August 2023 and June 2025.

title: Probable Loeys-Dietz Syndrome with aortic root dilatation and multiple arterial tortuosity in resource-limited setting : A case report.
abstract: Loeys-Dietz Syndrome (LDS) is a rare hereditary connective tissue disorder that is characterized by multisystem disorders predisposing individuals to arterial and aortic aneurysms. We present the case of a 17-year-old Bangladeshi male referred to cardiology for assessment of systemic abnormalities and cardiovascular risk. He presented with craniofacial, musculoskeletal, and cutaneous abnormalities including hypertelorism, mandibular ectopic hair, joint hypermobility with mild thoracic scoliosis, residual talipes equinovarus. He had past medical history of surgically corrected congenital anomalies. Based on clinical and radiological findings, he was diagnosed with clinically suspected Loeys-Dietz Syndrome as genetic testing was unavailable. He was managed through a multidisciplinary approach with regular follow-up. This report adds to literature on Loeys-Dietz Syndrome, emphasizing on aortic root dilatation and carotid artery tortuosity as important clinical and radiological features supporting diagnosis of LDS particularly in young patients presenting with characteristic craniofacial abnormalities or suggestive radiological findings. Early recognition and multidisciplinary management are crucial in resource-limited settings to prevent life-threatening vascular complications.

title: Cervical Spine Oncology: Perioperative Management and Complications.
abstract: STUDY DESIGN: Narrative review. OBJECTIVE: To synthesize contemporary evidence on perioperative complications in primary and metastatic cervical spine tumor surgery and to provide an evidence-informed framework for their prevention and management. SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Cervical spine tumor surgery converges dense neurovascular and aerodigestive anatomy with a medically fragile, frequently irradiated patient population. Although cervical metastases represent only about 8-20% of spinal metastatic disease, their mismanagement carries disproportionately severe consequences, ranging from disabling pain to high-level paralysis and death. Cervical-specific risk-stratification tools are lacking, and most available evidence is extrapolated from degenerative anterior cervical cohorts. METHODS: This is a narrative review of perioperative complications in cervical spine oncology. PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched for English-language articles published through May 2026, prioritizing literature from the past 5 years while including seminal earlier references where foundational, using combinations of the terms "cervical spine," "spinal metastasis," "spinal tumor," "perioperative complications," "airway," "vertebral artery," "wound," "dysphagia," "venous thromboembolism," and "hardware failure." Reference lists of included articles were hand-searched for additional sources. Studies were selected by author consensus for relevance to the complication domains discussed; formal risk-of-bias assessment and quantitative pooling were not performed, consistent with a narrative design. Because oncology-specific evidence is limited, data derived from degenerative cervical cohorts are identified as such throughout. RESULTS: Major complication domains include airway compromise (highest with multilevel corpectomy, combined approaches, and cervicothoracic constructs), vascular and neurologic injury, CSF leak, wound failure and infection in irradiated fields, hardware failure, venous thromboembolism, and dysphagia. CONCLUSIONS: Outcomes depend on preoperative risk stratification, multidisciplinary coordination, and individualized postoperative care rather than any single intraoperative maneuver. Because the evidence base remains largely Level III-IV without validated cervical oncology-specific tools, described practices should be regarded as reasonable, evidence-informed considerations rather than standards of care.

title: Age-dependent impact of diabetes on limb events and mortality in patients with peripheral artery disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is associated with substantial risks of limb events and mortality. Although diabetes is a recognized risk factor for adverse outcomes in PAD, its prognostic impact across different ages at PAD onset remains unclear. METHODS: In this retrospective population-based cohort study, adults with PAD were identified from Clalit Health Services, Israel (2000-2026). Patients were stratified by diabetes status and age at PAD diagnosis (35-50 vs > 50 years). The primary outcome was major adverse limb events (MALE), defined as lower-extremity revascularization or major amputation. All-cause mortality was a secondary outcome. Multivariable Cox regression, interaction analyses, and propensity score overlap weighting were performed. RESULTS: P P P P Among 4538 patients aged 35-50 years at PAD diagnosis, 1902 (42%) had diabetes. During a median follow-up of 12.0 years, diabetes was independently associated with higher risks of MALE (hazard ratio [HR] 1.44, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-2.01,= .032) and mortality (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.18-1.70,< .001). Diabetes was associated with increased MALE risk in both age groups, with no significant interaction by age (for interaction = .498). In contrast, the association between diabetes and mortality was significantly stronger in patients aged 35-50 years than in those aged >50 years (adjusted HR 2.00, 95% CI 1.72-2.33 vs 1.30, 95% CI 1.27-1.33,for interaction < .001). Excess mortality associated with diabetes emerged during longer-term follow-up. CONCLUSION: Diabetes was associated with increased risks of MALE and mortality in PAD, with a stronger association with mortality among patients diagnosed before age 50. These findings identify diabetes as a marker of particularly high risk in premature PAD.

Although diabetes is a recognized risk factor for adverse outcomes in PAD, its prognostic impact across different ages at PAD onset remains unclear. METHODS: In this retrospective population-based cohort study, adults with PAD were identified from Clalit Health Services, Israel (2000-2026).

title: Stent-graft placement for an axillosubclavian artery injury in a pediatric patient: A case report.
abstract: Axillosubclavian artery injury is a rare traumatic vascular injury associated with a high mortality rate. Therefore, rapid diagnosis and appropriate treatment selection are critical for patient survival. Although endovascular stent-graft placement has emerged as a less invasive alternative to open surgery, its application in pediatric trauma patients remains poorly documented. In this report, we present the case of a pediatric patient with traumatic axillosubclavian artery injury successfully treated with stent-graft placement. A 13-year-old boy was transported to a referring hospital following a traffic accident and transferred to our emergency and critical care center. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography conducted on hospital day 2 revealed a pseudoaneurysm due to right axillosubclavian artery injury, prompting endovascular stent-graft placement. The patient was discharged on hospital day 23. Although contrast-enhanced computed tomography at 1-year after discharge confirmed severe stenosis within the stent graft, distal perfusion was maintained. Notably, no ischemic symptoms or growth disturbances were observed in the right upper limb at the 3-year follow-up. Endovascular stent-graft placement appears to be a viable treatment for axillosubclavian artery injury in selected pediatric patients, particularly adolescents.

Therefore, rapid diagnosis and appropriate treatment selection are critical for patient survival. Although endovascular stent-graft placement has emerged as a less invasive alternative to open surgery, its application in pediatric trauma patients remains poorly documented.

title: Association between elevated lipoprotein (a) and venous thromboembolism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established cardiovascular risk factor linked to atherogenesis, inflammation, and thrombosis; however, its association with venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain, with inconsistent findings across observational studies. AIMS: To systematically evaluate the association between elevated Lp(a) levels and VTE risk and to examine differences by study design. METHODS: 2 2 PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception through January 2026 for observational studies assessing Lp(a) and VTE. Effect estimates (odds ratios [ORs] or hazard ratios [HRs]) were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Heterogeneity was assessed using Iand τ. Risk of bias was evaluated with ROBINS-E, publication bias with funnel plots, Egger's and Begg's tests, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. The primary outcome was VTE; secondary outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and recurrent VTE. RESULTS: 2 2 2 Eleven studies (6 case-control, 5 cohort; 63,325 participants; 3581 VTE events) were included. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a borderline increased VTE risk (pooled OR/HR 1.34 [95% CI 1.00-1.80]; P = 0.049), with high heterogeneity (I = 77.8%) and a wide prediction interval (0.56-3.21). In stratified analyses, case-control studies showed a significant association (OR 1.88 [1.25-2.81]; I = 57.2%), whereas cohort studies showed no association (HR 0.99 [0.85-1.15]; I = 0%), with significant between-group differences (p < 0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: The association between elevated Lp(a) and VTE appears limited to case-control studies and is not supported by prospective cohort data, suggesting potential bias or residual confounding. Further large-scale and genetic studies are warranted to clarify this relationship.

title: Ultralow-contrast stepping digital subtraction angiography for whole-limb arterial evaluation: A case report.
abstract: Stepping digital subtraction angiography (DSA) enables whole-limb arterial assessment with a single contrast injection, and diluted contrast medium may further reduce iodine exposure. A patient in their 80s with an abdominal aortic aneurysm and bilateral common iliac artery aneurysms was scheduled for staged internal iliac artery embolization before endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). Due to a mural thrombus in the left common iliac artery aneurysm, right internal iliac artery embolization was performed via an ipsilateral approach. Severe right external iliac artery stenosis prompted stepping DSA before and after embolization to evaluate distal embolization. Sevenfold- and tenfold-diluted stepping DSA examinations were performed before and after embolization, respectively, using identical injection parameters (3 mL/s; 30 mL). These required 4.29 and 3.0 mL of undiluted contrast medium, respectively. Although pedal artery enhancement was reduced with tenfold dilution, image quality remained acceptable, and no obvious distal embolization was identified in the visualized arteries; however, small emboli in poorly opacified pedal branches could not be excluded with tenfold dilution. Because internal iliac artery embolization was not expected to significantly alter lower-extremity arterial perfusion, the observed difference in image quality was considered to primarily reflect the difference between the two dilution protocols rather than changes in arterial hemodynamics. Ultralow-contrast stepping DSA may be a contrast-saving technique in selected cases when repeated whole-limb arterial evaluation is required.

A patient in their 80s with an abdominal aortic aneurysm and bilateral common iliac artery aneurysms was scheduled for staged internal iliac artery embolization before endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). Due to a mural thrombus in the left common iliac artery aneurysm, right internal iliac artery embolization was performed via an ipsilateral approach.

title: A Novel Hybrid Endovascular Technique for Tympanojugular Paraganglioma: Flow Diversion Followed by Direct Transauricular Squid Embolization.
abstract: Skull-base paragangliomas with persistent internal carotid artery (ICA) supply can be challenging to devascularize safely. We report a 17-yearold male with an Succinate Dehydrogenase Complex Iron Sulfur Subunit B (SDHB)-associated tympanojugular paraganglioma treated using a staged hybrid endovascular strategy after subtotal resection. Persistent supply from a short ICA feeder and circumferential involvement of the petrous ICA precluded safe conventional transarterial embolization. A Surpass Elite flow-diverting stent was deployed across the feeder after dual antiplatelet therapy to preserve parent-vessel patency, reduce tumour inflow, and reinforce the arterial wall. Four months later, protected direct transauricular and transcervical puncture embolization with Squid 12 was performed under intermittent ICA balloon occlusion. Marked tumor devascularization was achieved without embolic or thromboembolic complication, and definitive resection was completed without new neurological or cranial nerve deficit. This staged approach may provide a useful adjunct for selected skull-base paragangliomas with persistent ICA supply when conventional embolization carries unacceptable risk.

title: Association of Estimated Arterial Stiffness with Collateral Status and Functional Outcome after Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Secondary Analysis of the OPTIMAL-BP Trial.
abstract: PURPOSE: Estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) is a surrogate of arterial stiffness that may influence stroke outcomes and potentially affect collateral circulation. We examined the association of ePWV with collateral status and 3-month functional outcome after successful endovascular thrombectomy and explored the contribution of collateral status to this relationship across blood pressure (BP) management strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this secondary analysis of the Outcome in Patients Treated With Intra-Arterial Thrombectomy-Optimal Blood Pressure Control trial, 285 patients were analyzed. Collateral status was assessed using the Tan scale (poor, 0-1; good, 2-3). Poor functional outcome was defined as 3-month modified Rankin Scale score of 3-6. Multivariable logistic and mediation analyses were performed to evaluate the association between ePWV and functional outcomes and to explore direct and indirect pathways. RESULTS: A total of 285 patients were included (mean age, 73.3±11.3 years; 40.4% women). Each 1 m/s increase in ePWV was associated with poor collaterals (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1.276, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.083-1.503) and poor functional outcome (adjusted OR 1.338, 95% CI 1.121-1.597). In mediation analyses, collateral status accounted for only a small proportion of the association between ePWV and poor functional outcome (indirect effect: adjusted β 0.022, 95% CI 0.001-0.053), whereas the direct effect remained significant (adjusted β 0.237, 95% CI 0.115-0.359). Neither the direct effect of ePWV on functional outcome nor the indirect effect through collateral status differed according to BP management strategy. CONCLUSION: Higher ePWV was associated with poor collateral status and unfavorable functional outcome after successful reperfusion. Collateral status accounted for only a small proportion of the observed association between ePWV and functional outcome.

We examined the association of ePWV with collateral status and 3-month functional outcome after successful endovascular thrombectomy and explored the contribution of collateral status to this relationship across blood pressure (BP) management strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this secondary analysis of the Outcome in Patients Treated With Intra-Arterial Thrombectomy-Optimal Blood Pressure Control trial, 285 patients were analyzed.

title: Early outcomes of the Octapro balloon-expandable transcatheter heart valve in an unrestricted cohort of patients with aortic valve stenosis: the MyPro registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Data on early outcomes of the novel balloon-expandable (BE) Octapro transcatheter heart valve (THV) in real-world practice are limited. We sought to assess procedural safety and early outcomes of the Octapro in patients with severe native aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). METHODS: Between November 2024 and October 2025, consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI with Octapro in European and Indian centres were enrolled. Primary endpoints were VARC-3 technical success, device success, and early safety at 30-day. RESULTS: 2 A total of 303 patients were included (age 78.9 ± 7.4 years; bicuspid 13%). VARC-3 technical success was 97%, peri-procedural mortality 0.3% while no procedural stroke or myocardial infarction were reported. In-hospital guidelines-indicated permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) rate was 13.5%. At discharge mean gradient was 8.4 ± 4.5 mmHg, effective orifice area 1.8 ± 0.3 cm, while moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak was reported in 3.3% of the patients. At 30-day, device success was 92.4% and early safety 80%. All-cause mortality was 2.6%, stroke 0.3%, and guidelines-indicated PPI 14.2%. Mean gradient remained low (9 ± 4 mmHg). Implantation depth and baseline right bundle branch block (RBBB) were independent predictors of PPI. ROC analysis identified an implantation depth threshold of 4.75 mm associated with increased PPI risk. CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world registry, the Octapro THV demonstrated high procedural success, favourable early clinical outcomes, and excellent haemodynamic performance. Implantation depth and baseline RBBB were independent predictors of PPI, supporting optimization of implantation technique to mitigate conduction disturbances.

We sought to assess procedural safety and early outcomes of the Octapro in patients with severe native aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). METHODS: Between November 2024 and October 2025, consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI with Octapro in European and Indian centres were enrolled.

title: Transcatheter mitral valve implantation in complex anatomies: Outcomes after prior repair or aborted interventions.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with recurrent mitral valve disease after prior repair or persistent disease following an aborted edge-to-edge repair attempt face high risks with conventional surgery. The outcomes of transcatheter mitral valve implantation (TMVI) in these distinct cohorts remain unclear. METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included all patients undergoing Tendyne-TMVI between June 2020 and December 2024 for recurrent mitral valve disease after TEER, SMA, balloon valvuloplasty, or persistent mitral valve disease after aborted TEER. Outcomes were assessed using MVARC criteria. RESULTS: Of 85 TMVI procedures, 16 were included (median age 80 years (IQR 70-83); STS 6.9% (IQR 5.6-8.2)). Prior interventions were SMA (37.5%), TEER (12.5%), balloon valvuloplasty (6.2%) and aborted TEER (43.8%). Technical success was 93.8%. At discharge, all patients showed none/trace residual mitral or paravalvular regurgitation, with a mean gradient of 3.9 ± 1.1 mmHg. At 30 days, one patient presented with severe paravalvular regurgitation due to atrialization of the prosthetic valve; no stroke occurred. Acute renal failure requiring dialysis occurred in 18.8%, one major bleeding and rehospitalization for heart failure in 12.5%. Thirty-day mortality was 12.5%. NYHA class improved significantly from 3 to 2 (p = 0.042). MVARC device success at 30 days was 63%. Estimated 1- and 2-year survival was 67% and 56% with 50% of deaths being non-cardiovascular. CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected high-risk patients with recurrent or persistent mitral valve disease, Tendyne TMVI achieved durable prosthetic mitral valve function, leading to significant symptomatic improvement. Failure to meet device success was mainly driven by mean mitral gradients exceeding 5 mmHg.

title: Long-term cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in Turner syndrome patients with congenital heart disease: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Congenital cardiac anomalies are a major determinant of morbidity and mortality in Turner syndrome (TS), yet long-term cardiovascular outcome data remain limited. This study assessed cardiovascular morbidity, mortality, valve dysfunction, and aortic outcomes in TS patients with congenital cardiovascular defects. METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 84 TS patients with congenital cardiovascular anomalies were analyzed, with follow-up between 01/1980 and 01/2025. Clinical, demographic, electrocardiographic and echocardiographic variables were reviewed; morbidity and mortality were recorded; descriptive statistics applied. RESULTS: 2 Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) was present in 40 patients (48%) and coarctation of the aorta (CoA) in 29 (35%); 19 patients (23%) had both. At last follow-up (median age 26 years, IQR 31 years), most patients were in NYHA class I (82%) and mean systolic and diastolic blood pressure were 121.7 ± 16.8 mmHg and 76.1 ± 13.1 mmHg, respectively. Sinus rhythm was present in 96% of the patients. In the BAV cohort, aortic regurgitation increased from 6 patients (15%) at first registration to 17 (42.5%) at last follow-up. In the tricuspid aortic valve cohort, aortic regurgitation increased from 1 patient (2.3%) to 12 (27.9%). The last mean ascending aortic diameter indexed to body surface area was 20.4 ± 4.6 mm/m. Aortic dissection occurred in 2 patients (2.7%). Ten patients died during follow-up; median age at death was 41 years (IQR: 52 years), and cardiac causes accounted for at least 50% of mortality. CONCLUSION: BAV and CoA predominated in this TS cohort. Despite generally favorable functional status among survivors, progressive valve dysfunction, aortic complications and cardiovascular mortality support lifelong structured surveillance.

This study assessed cardiovascular morbidity, mortality, valve dysfunction, and aortic outcomes in TS patients with congenital cardiovascular defects. METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 84 TS patients with congenital cardiovascular anomalies were analyzed, with follow-up between 01/1980 and 01/2025.

title: Analysis of risk factors and construction of a prediction model for postoperative deep vein thrombosis in patients with periarticular knee fractures.
abstract: The present study aimed to identify risk factors for postoperative deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in patients with periarticular knee fractures. A prediction model was constructed for the early identification of high-risk patients. Data from 319 patients at who underwent surgery at the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University (Luzhou, China) between January 2020 and December 2022 were analyzed. Based on ultrasound results, patients were divided into a DVT group (n=83) and a non-DVT group (n=236). Logistic regression was employed to identify independent risk factors. Subsequently, a nomogram model was established, which was validated via receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). The DVT rate was 26.0%. Old age (OR, 1.0228), high American Society of Anesthesiologists grade (OR, 2.2764), greater blood loss (OR, 1.0015), blood transfusion (OR, 2.7917) and high D-dimer levels (OR, 1.0251) were identified as independent risk factors (P<0.05), while living in cities, high hemoglobin, high prealbumin, high Barthel index and high Braden scores served as protective factors (P<0.05). The model yielded an area under the curve value of 0.837. Additionally, the calibration curve showed high accuracy, and DCA validated the favorable clinical applicability of this predictive model. In conclusion, the model performs well in helping doctors to identify high-risk patients and optimize individualized therapeutic strategies.
